44.06.additionalInfo: You can combine with Jian Feng (44) and Jian Zhong2 (44) using the Dao Ma needling technique to improve results. One of Master Tung's 72 absolute needles for treating knee disorders. Hu Wen Zhi To treat gout and migratory arthritis, you can use 44.06 Jian Zhong, Jian Zhong2 (44), 77.18 Shen Guan, 88.01 Tong Guan, and 88.03 Tong Tian. Knee 44.06 Jian Zhong is important for treating knee disorders for two reasons. The first reason is that in Master Tung's acupuncture, many points that affect the heart also affect the knee, primarily because the heart channel in the thigh passes through the center of the knee. Therefore, since this point innervates the heart, it is important for treating knee disorders. The second reason is that in Master Tung's acupuncture, the shoulder is used to treat knee disorders. 44.06 Jian Zhong treats the center of the knee (the heart channel passes through the center of the knee), pain inside the knee, and pain above and below the patella, and it can be combined with Zhong Jian2 (44) and Jian Feng (44). The lateral side of the shoulder treats the medial aspect of the knee because the liver channel passes through the medial aspect of the knee, while in the arm, it passes through the lateral side. You can combine 44.06 Jian Zhong with 44.15 Xia Qu and 44.16 Shang Qu (liver channel) to treat medial knee pain. Likewise, the medial side of the shoulder treats the lateral aspect of the knee because the lung channel in Master Tung's acupuncture passes through the lateral side of the knee, while in the arm, it passes through the medial side. You can combine 44.06 Jian Zhong with 44.11 Yun Bai and 44.12 Li Bai (lung channel) to treat lateral knee pain. Six Shoulder Points - Liu Jian A combination of six points located in the shoulder can treat a wide range of disorders. The six points are: 44.06 Jian Zhong, Jian Zhong2 (44) (heart channel). 44.11 Yun Bai, 44.12 Li Bai (lung channel). 44.15 Xia Qu, 44.16 Shang Xu (liver channel). The indications for the six shoulder points can be divided into three categories: Head, face, and sensory organ disorders: Occipital and frontal headache, itchy, red, swollen eyes, trigeminal neuralgia, toothache, and facial paralysis. Neck, shoulder, upper and lower back, lower limb disorders: Neck pain, cervical vertebrae disorders, back pain, stroke, knee pain, hip joint pain, ankle sprain, leg pain, shoulder pain, polio. 44.08.additionalInfo: The point is used to treat spleen, liver, and gallbladder diseases. For additional information, see 44.10 Tian Zong. Point Name Rén [Al — Zöng [m] person. —sect, clan, ancestor, family. Rén [Al — person. Zöng [N — sect, clan, ancestor, family. To further appreciate the significance of these points, it's helpful to consider traditional Chinese culture, where the concept of the Ancestor (Zong - ) is deeply rooted in the philosophy of filial piety (Xiao - ). This tradition is not about religious worship, but rather about paying deep respect (Bai - ) to the absolute root and foundation of one's lineage. It acknowledges that an unbroken river flows continuously from a single foundational spring, and a system can only survive and maintain its flow if its roots are honored and protected. Expanding on this cultural perspective, Master Tung deliberately chose the name Zong to hint at the hidden mechanism of action of these points. By mapping the philosophy of the "Ancestor" onto human anatomy, the chest is seen as the body's primary source. The character Zong ( ) points directly to Zong Qi ( — Gathering/AncestraI Qi), the foundational energy in the chest controlled by the lungs and heart. This Qi is the main driver of Qi and Blood movement in the body. As a family depends on its roots, the body relies on Zong Qi to keep blood and energy moving. By using this chest energy, these points strongly affect the heart and lungs. In emergencies, needling these points helps restore the flow of Qi and Blood, bringing vital life rhythms back. The characters Tian (Heaven — Di (Earth — itt and Ren (Human — ) represent the vertical hierarchy of the points along the bicipital groove of the upper arm, with each corresponding to a distinct level of Zong Qi distribution: Ren Zong (Human Ancestor — The Bottom Point): Situated lowest on the arm. Di Zong (Earth Ancestor — The Middle Point): Situated in the center of the arm. Tian Zong (Heaven Ancestor — The Top Point): Situated highest on the arm near the shoulder.

44.12.additionalInfo: For more information, see 44.11 Yun Bai. San Jin (44), 44.08 Ren Zong, 44.09 Di Zong, 44.10 Tian Zong, 44.12 Li Bai, 44.11 Yun Bail and Shang Yun Bai (44) are all located on the same vertical line, which represents the lung channel in Master Tung's acupuncture. Among the six shoulder points (Liu Jian), 44.12 Li Bai is the best for treating hyperhidrosis. 44.06 Jian Zhong, 44.11 Yun Bai, and 44.12 Li Bai treat pain in the lateral part of the knee. Hu Wen Zi Li Bai with 44.01 Yun Bai creates a special effect for treating foot sprains. Point Name Li [$1 — Plum. Båi [ä] — white. Li — Plum. Bai ( - White): In the Five Phases, White corresponds to Metal and the Lungs. The Lungs govern the Qi, the skin, the exterior, and the opening/closing of the pores. This perfectly explains why the point is so effective for treating hyperhidrosis (excessive sweating) and body odor. "White" also clinically hints at the white discharge (leukorrhea) that this point group treats in gynecology. Li ( - Plum): In Chinese Medicine, the plum is associated with a sour flavor. The sour flavor corresponds to the Wood element and the Liver. What does the Liver govern in the body? The tendons and sinews. The Synergy (Metal controlling Wood): When you put "Plum" (Wood/ Tendons) and "White" (Metal/Qi) together, it represents the energetic dynamic of Metal controlling Wood. By needling Li Bai, you are using strong Lung Qi to regulate the Liver and relax the tendons. This is the exact physiological reason why Li Bai is a "special effect" for severe foot — white. sprains, lower-leg pain, and polio.

44.17.additionalInfo: Shaun Goodman 44.17 Shui Yu Er/San: This treatment treats lower back pain adjacent to the spine, pain in the posterior buttocks, and hip joint pain. The 12 Shoulder Needles A combination of 12 points located on the lung, heart, liver, and kidney channels in Master Tung's acupuncture. Lung Channel: Shang Yun Bai (44), 44.11 Yun Bair 44.12 Li Bai. Heart Channel: Jian Feng (44), 44.06 Jian Zhong, Jian Zhong2 (44). Liver Channel: Shang Qu Shang (44), 44.16 Shang Qu, 44.15 Xia Qu. Kidney Channel: 44.17 Shui Yu, Shui Yu Er (44), Shui Yu san (44) The 12 Shoulder points affect the pelvic area, lower back, and lower abdomen. These points can be used for disorders in these areas, such as lower back pain, urinary system disorders, and gynecological disorders causing pain in the area. It is not necessary to needle all 12 points; the needle is according to the location of the pain. The points on the kidney channel affect the area near the spine and sacrum. The points on the liver channel affect the posterior aspect, which is the back side of the lower back and pelvis (buttocks). The points on the heart channel affect the lateral aspect: the side of the lower back and hip area. The points on the lung channel affect the anterior aspect: the lower abdomen and anterior pelvis. San Jian Liao (DT) can be added to affect the sacrum. Point Name Shui [7k] — Water. Yü — Heal. The point's name suggests its ability to treat kidney-related issues and lower back pain. SanZhengJi.additionalInfo: San Zheng Ji (44) is located on the same vertical line as Jian Zhong2 (44), 44.06 Jian Zhong, and Jian Feng (44) on the heart channel in the acupuncture system of Master Tung. The heart channel influences the center of the body and the organs in the center, such as the stomach, heart, and, in the case of San Zheng Ji — the spine. Additionally, the channel passes through the lateral part of the arm, so the points on the channel can treat pain in the lateral part of the thigh. Pain along the lateral side of the thigh can be combined with Jian Zhong (44.06), Jian Feng (44), and Jian Zhong2 (44). They are three of the 72 Absolute Needles of DongTung, which are used to treat spinal disorders, especially those of the lower spine.
